requirement: Standardize a feature matrix column by column for model training when some cells are missing and some features are constant.
skeleton: standardize converting input to float64, rejecting non 2-D arrays, and dividing centered data by the nan-aware sample std with zero std replaced by 1.
caption: Column-wise z-scores with NumPy that survive missing values and constant features. standardize(x) converts x with np.asarray to float64, so lists and integer arrays work and the input is never modified, and raises ValueError mentioning 2-D when the array is not two dimensional. It computes per-column np.nanmean and np.nanstd with ddof 1, the sample standard deviation, both along axis 0 so NaN cells are ignored. Columns whose std is zero divide by 1 via np.where so they become 0 without a divide warning, and NaN cells remain NaN in the output. The fixture asserts that columns 1, 2, 3 and 10, 20, 30 both become -1, 0, 1, that a NaN cell stays NaN while its column standardizes to plus and minus the square root of one half, that a constant column is all zero with warnings as errors, that 1-D input raises ValueError, and that the input array is unchanged.

plan.intent: Preprocess features before fitting a model
constraints: Means and stds are per column and ignore NaN
NaN cells stay NaN and the input is not modified

rationale.teaches: Use nan-aware reductions along the right axis with the intended ddof and guard zero variance explicitly instead of letting NaN or inf leak.
rationale.why: A plain mean turns a column with one gap into all NaN, population std shifts every score, and dividing by zero std floods the matrix with NaN.

ops.docstring: Standardize feature columns with NumPy, tolerating NaN and constant columns.

ops.source:
def standardize(x: ArrayLike) -> NDArray[np.float64]:
    """Return per-column z-scores using the sample std; NaN cells stay NaN."""
    data = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
    if data.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError(f"expected a 2-D array, got {data.ndim}-D")
    mean = np.nanmean(data, axis=0)
    std = np.nanstd(data, axis=0, ddof=1)
    safe = np.where(std > 0, std, 1.0)
    return (data - mean) / safe

candidates.why_wrong: One missing cell turns its whole column into NaN.
Population std is used, so scores are scaled by the wrong factor.
Constant columns divide by zero and become NaN with warnings.
1-D input is standardized silently instead of being rejected.
A single global mean is subtracted instead of one mean per column.
